does: Cooks sausages in a little fat over a moderate heat, turning them often, so that the skin browns evenly all round while the inside cooks without the skin bursting.
how: Heat a little oil in a frying pan over a medium-low heat.
Lay the sausages in with space between them. Do not prick them.
Turn them every so often, so that each side browns in turn.
To brown them only, for a dish that finishes them in a sauce or the oven, stop once they are coloured all over.

cues.text: An even, deep brown skin all round, sticky and glossy, with no pale stripes.
A gentle, steady sizzle, never a fierce spitting.

mistakes.mistake: Frying over a high heat, so that the skins split and burn before the middle is done.
mistakes.fix: Keep the heat moderate and give them time.

mistakes.mistake: Pricking the skins, so that the fat and juice run out and the sausages turn dry.
mistakes.fix: Leave the skins whole; a moderate heat keeps them from bursting.

variant_of.differs: The sausages are round, so they are turned many times over a long, moderate fry rather than once, and the skin is kept whole.
